sentence: Juno's 2022 microwave radiometer flyby measured Europa's ice shell at about 29 kilometers thick, plus or minus 10 kilometers, under a pure water-ice assumption.
source: Levin et al., 'Europa's ice thickness and subsurface structure characterized by the Juno microwave radiometer', Nature Astronomy, 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41550-025-02718-0

sentence: Cassini CDA measured sodium phosphates in Enceladus ice grains; inferred ocean phosphorus is at least about 100 times Earth's ocean concentration.
source: Postberg et al., 'Detection of phosphates originating from Enceladus's ocean', Nature, 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-05987-9

sentence: Cassini INMS detected molecular hydrogen (H2) in Enceladus's plume, consistent with hydrothermal water-rock reactions below the ice.
source: Waite et al., 'Cassini finds molecular hydrogen in the Enceladus plume: Evidence for hydrothermal processes', Science, 2017, DOI 10.1126/science.aai8703

sentence: Europa's subsurface ocean contains more than twice the water of all Earth's oceans combined.
source: NASA Europa Clipper mission overview, NASA Science (science.nasa.gov/mission/europa-clipper)

sentence: Freshly ejected Enceladus ice grains contain organic fragments; some nitrogen- and oxygen-containing identifications are tentative.
source: Khawaja et al., 'Detection of organic compounds in freshly ejected ice grains from Enceladus's ocean', Nature Astronomy, 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41550-025-02655-y

sentence: Europa Clipper launched October 14, 2024; Mars gravity assist March 1, 2025; Earth gravity assist December 3, 2026; Jupiter orbit April 2030; first Europa flyby March 7, 2031.
source: NASA Europa Clipper mission timeline, NASA Science

sentence: Europa Clipper orbits Jupiter and will make 49 close flybys of Europa; it will not land.
source: NASA Europa Clipper mission overview, NASA Science
